title: Kelan matkakorvausmenot kasvoivat, taustalla etenkin arvonlisäveron ja taksitaksan korotukset
supports: Kela paid 364 M€ travel reimbursement in 2025 for 4.6 M trips, 3.3 M of them by taxi
quote: Kela maksoi vuonna 2025 matkakorvauksia 364 miljoonaa euroa yhteensä 4,6 miljoonasta matkasta. Matkoista 3,3 miljoonaa oli taksimatkoja.
note: EN: In 2025 Kela paid 364 million euros of travel reimbursement for 4.6 million trips; 3.3 million were taxi trips. Published 9.4.2026. (Page also: 3.8 M taxi trips in total, of which 3.3 M exceeded the copayment.)

title: Kelan matkakorvausmenot kasvoivat (taxi spend)
supports: Taxi reimbursement in 2025 was 227 M€
quote: Kela maksoi taksimatkoista 227 miljoonaa euroa korvauksia 390 000 henkilölle.
note: EN: Kela paid 227 million euros of reimbursement for taxi trips to 390,000 people (2025).

title: Kelan matkakorvausmenot kasvoivat (per-resident spend)
supports: Highest travel reimbursement per resident Kainuu 157 €, lowest Helsinki 23 € (2025)
quote: Suurin euromääräinen korvaus oli 157 euroa per asukas Kainuussa ja pienin 23 euroa per asukas Helsingissä.
note: EN: The largest reimbursement was 157 euros per resident in Kainuu and the smallest 23 euros per resident in Helsinki.

title: Matkakorvaukset
supports: Patient copayment is at most 25 € per one-way trip
quote: Omavastuu yhdensuuntaiselta matkalta on enintään 25 euroa.
note: EN: The copayment for a one-way trip is at most 25 euros. The spec's English URL https://kela.fi/reimbursements-of-travel-costs-copayment returned 'page not found' on 2026-11-14; cite www.kela.fi/matkat instead.

title: Matkakorvaukset (vuosiomavastuu)
supports: Annual travel copayment cap is 300 €
quote: Tähän 300 euron vuosiomavastuuseen lasketaan mukaan kaikki yksittäisten matkojen 25 euroa ja tätä pienemmät omavastuut.
note: EN: All single-trip copayments of 25 euros or less count towards this 300-euro annual copayment cap.

title: Matkakorvaukset (oma auto)
supports: Own-car travel is reimbursed at 0.33 €/km
quote: Jos käytät omaa tai toisen omistamaa autoa, korvaus on 0,33 e/km.
note: EN: If you use your own or someone else's car, the reimbursement is 0.33 €/km. Caveat: the same page says Kela pays 0.33 €/km only on the part of the cost exceeding the 25 € copayment, so km × 0.33 is a cost basis, not the net payout. Also confirmed on Kela partner page (kela_oma_auto.txt).

title: Matkakorvaukset (yöpymisraha)
supports: Overnight allowance is up to 20.18 € per night
quote: Yöpymisrahaa maksetaan vuorokaudessa enintään 20,18 euroa.
note: EN: The overnight allowance is at most 20.18 euros per day. Same figure on the plain-language page https://www.kela.fi/web/selkokieli/korvaukset-matkoista ('Se on enintään 20,18 euroa vuorokaudessa.').

title: Korvaukset matkoista (selkokieli)
supports: Overnight allowance 20.18 €/day; 25 € copayment; 300 € annual cap (plain-language page from spec)
quote: Se on enintään 20,18 euroa vuorokaudessa.
note: EN: It is at most 20.18 euros per day (overnight allowance). Page also states the 25 € one-way copayment and 300 € annual cap.

title: Hypofractionated breast radiotherapy for 1 week versus 3 weeks (FAST-Forward): 5-year efficacy and late normal tissue effects results from a multicentre, non-inferiority, randomised, phase 3 trial
supports: 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week is non-inferior to 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks (4,096 patients)
quote: 26 Gy in five fractions over 1 week is non-inferior to the standard of 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks
note: Murray Brunt A, Haviland JS, Wheatley DA, et al. Lancet 2020;395(10237):1613-1626. PMID 32580883. Abstract also: 'we recruited and obtained consent from 4096 patients from 97 UK centres'. Abstract text from Europe PMC REST API.

title: FAST-Forward 2020 (sample size)
supports: FAST-Forward randomised 4,096 patients
quote: we recruited and obtained consent from 4096 patients from 97 UK centres

title: Hypofractionated breast radiotherapy for 1 week versus 3 weeks (FAST-Forward): 10-year efficacy and late normal tissue effects from a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, phase 3, randomised controlled trial and 5-year efficacy results from a randomised axillary substudy
supports: 10-year ipsilateral breast recurrence 2.1% after 26 Gy/5 fractions vs 3.6% after 40 Gy/15 fractions
quote: 3·6% (95% CI 2·7-4·9) for the 40 Gy group, 2·9% (2·1-4·0) for the 27 Gy group, and 2·1% (1·5-3·1) for the 26 Gy group
note: Brunt AM, Cafferty FH, Kirby AM, Patel J, Sydenham MA, Haviland JS, ... Yarnold JR, Bliss JM. Lancet Oncol 2026;27(6):686-698, first published 2026-05-14. PMID 42134381. 10-year ITT population n=4087 (4110 enrolled, 23 withdrew data consent). Interpretation: 'Long-term follow-up confirms that 26 Gy in five fractions over 1 week is safe and efficacious ... supporting its use as a standard of care.' Late moderate/marked breast effects 13.1% (40 Gy) vs 14.4% (26 Gy).

title: FAST-Forward 10-year (interpretation)
supports: 26 Gy/5 fractions is safe and efficacious long term, supporting its use as a standard of care
quote: Long-term follow-up confirms that 26 Gy in five fractions over 1 week is safe and efficacious for adjuvant radiotherapy to the breast or chest wall
note: Same paper as fastforward_10y_2026; next words: 'supporting its use as a standard of care'. Nodal substudy: efficacy 'reassuring' but limited precision.

title: One-Week Radiotherapy for Breast Cancer Safe, Effective Up to 10 Years
supports: ESTRO 2025 presentation of FAST-Forward 10-year results: similar level of cancer control
quote: The shorter radiotherapy schedule provides a similar level of cancer control to standard treatment, with no additional long-term side effects observed.
note: Published 27 May 2025. CAVEAT: HealthDay reports 2.0% recurrence for 26 Gy/5 Fr (vs 3.6% for 40 Gy/15 Fr); the published Lancet Oncology paper gives 2.1%. Use the paper's 2.1%.

title: One week of radiotherapy just as good as three for early-stage breast cancer
supports: Press coverage of FAST-Forward 10-year results (2.1% vs 3.6%)
note: NOT FETCHED: irishnews.com is blocked by the session proxy. Could not verify any text. DROP this source; the Lancet Oncology paper (fastforward_10y_2026) and HealthDay cover the same facts.

title: Radiotherapy dose fractionation, fourth edition: 03 Breast cancer
supports: 15 fractions (40 Gy/15) remains the recommended schedule for regional nodal irradiation
quote: For regional nodal irradiation: • 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks (Grade B)
note: Recommendation box on PDF page 9 (printed page 23 of the RCR fourth edition). PDF created Jan 2024.

title: Radiotherapy dose fractionation, fourth edition: 03 Breast cancer
supports: 26 Gy/5 fractions is recommended for non-nodal breast or chest wall radiotherapy
quote: For adjuvant radiotherapy of non-nodal breast or chest wall without immediate reconstruction: • 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week (Grade A)
note: Recommendation box on PDF page 3 (printed page 17). Defines the eligible group: non-nodal whole breast/chest wall without immediate reconstruction.

title: Assessing the utilization of radiotherapy near end of life at a Finnish University Hospital: a retrospective cohort study
supports: Turku University Hospital 2005-2013: single-fraction RT used in only 7% of courses in the last year of life
quote: During the last year of life single-fraction treatment was used only in 7% of all therapy courses.
note: Rautakorpi LK, et al. Acta Oncol 2017;56(10). DOI 10.1080/0284186X.2017.1324638, PMID 28503990. CAVEAT: 7% is of ALL radiotherapy courses in the last year of life (any indication), not specifically bone metastases; single centre (TUH), 2005-2013.

title: Real-life perspectives on the end-of-life care of cancer patients (doctoral thesis, Annales D 1636)
supports: Turku: patients living >100 km from the hospital were treated least often near death (median 110 days from last RT to death vs 80-83 days for others)
quote: Patients living >100 km from the hospital were treated least frequently near death and had a median of 110 days to death
note: PDF page 47 (printed page 45). Continues: 'and had a median of 110 days to death from the last treatment. For other groups it was 80–83 days.' English abstract (PDF page 6): 'longer for patients living >100km from TUH'.

title: Päijät-Hämeen hyvinvointialue: Uusi sädehoitolaite vahvistaa syövänhoitoa
supports: Päijät-Häme Central Hospital (Lahti) has a radiotherapy unit

note: EN: A new state-of-the-art radiotherapy machine has been taken into use in the radiotherapy unit of Päijät-Häme Central Hospital. Press release dated 19.8.2026. Also: 'Sädehoitopotilaat käyvät hoidossa usein päivittäin useiden viikkojen ajan' (patients often attend daily for several weeks).

note: EN: Radiotherapy patients often attend treatment daily for several weeks.

note: EN: With a few exceptions, the radiotherapy unit is responsible for radiotherapy of all adult and paediatric patients of Pirkanmaa and most of Kanta-Häme and part of South Ostrobothnia wellbeing services counties. note: EN: For part of the population the trip to the nearest central hospital is over 400 km and to the nearest university hospital over 700 km. PDF page 13 = printed page 13.

title: Geographical distance and reduced access to palliative radiotherapy: systematic review and meta-analysis
supports: Living ≥50 km from an RT centre: 16% lower odds of palliative RT (OR 0.84)
quote: living ≥50 km vs <50 km from the radiotherapy centre was associated with a reduced likelihood of receiving PRT (OR 0.84 (95%CI 0.80, 0.88))
note: Chand CP, Greenley S, Macleod U, Lind M, Barton R, Kelly C. BMJ Support Palliat Care 2022. DOI 10.1136/bmjspcare-2021-003356, PMID 35292512. OR 0.84 = 16% lower odds. Quote from Europe PMC abstract; the Hull repository URL (spec) is unreachable from this session (Cloudflare / host not allowed), so the match of record 3916737 to this paper is inferred from title/authors (Hull York Medical School), not confirmed. Prefer the DOI URL https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjspcare-2021-003356.

title: Area-based disparities in non-small-cell lung cancer survival
supports: NSCLC patients living >50 km from Vaasa Central Hospital had adjusted death hazard 1.47
quote: the adjusted HR increased to 1.47 (95% CI: 1.07–2.01; p = 0.017) for patients living in rural areas compared to those in urban areas
note: Paakkola N-M, et al. Acta Oncol 2024;63:146-153. DOI 10.2340/1651-226X.2024.27507. Rural = >50 km from Vaasa Central Hospital (postal code); n=321, 2016-2020; adjusted for performance status, frailty and stage. CAVEAT: distance is to the hospital (not specifically a radiotherapy unit); outcome is overall survival.

title: Factors influencing access to palliative radiotherapy: a Norwegian population-based study
supports: Source cited by the roadmap for the 100 km fact (Norway): travel distance 100-499 km associated with less palliative RT
quote: Patients with low education, those living in certain counties, or with travel distances 100-499 km, were also less likely to receive PRT.
note: Åsli LM, et al. Acta Oncol 2018;57(9):1250-1258. PMID 29706109. Norwegian data, 2009-2011 deaths. Quote from Europe PMC abstract.

title: Update of the systematic review of palliative radiation therapy fractionation for bone metastases
supports: Retreatment 20% after single fraction vs 8% after multiple fractions
quote: with 20% receiving additional treatment to the same site versus 8% in the multiple fraction treatment arm
note: Rich SE, Chow R, Raman S, Liang Zeng K, Lutz S, Lam H, Silva MF, Chow E. Radiother Oncol 2018;126(3):547-557. PMID 29397209. Meta-analysis of 29 RCTs; preceding words: 'Re-treatment was significantly more frequent in the single fraction treatment arm'; p < 0.01. Corrigendum published 2019 (PMID 30981439) - content of corrigendum not checked.

title: Update of the systematic review of palliative radiation therapy fractionation for bone metastases
supports: Pain response similar for single vs multiple fractions (61% vs 62%)
quote: the overall response rate was similar in patients for single fraction treatments (61%; 1867/3059) and those for multiple fraction treatments (62%; 1890/3040)
note: Intention-to-treat; complete response 23% vs 24%. PMID 29397209.

title: Update on the systematic review of palliative radiotherapy trials for bone metastases
supports: Single and multiple fractions give equal pain relief; retreatment higher after single fraction
quote: Single and multiple fraction regimens provided equal pain relief; however, significantly higher retreatment rates occurred in those receiving single fractions.
note: Chow E, Zeng L, Salvo N, Dennis K, Tsao M, Lutz S. Clin Oncol (R Coll Radiol) 2012;24(2):112-124. PMID 22130630. 25 RCTs; retreatment 2.6-fold more likely after single fraction (abstract does not give the % rates; use Rich 2018 for 20% vs 8%).
